title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (section V, 'Données préliminaires', continued from p.547). G is a profinite group with a surjection from GL(2,Z)^ ≅ T^±_{1,1}, the profinite extended Teichmüller (mapping class) group of type (1,1). It is generated topologically by the images of ρ (order 6), σ (order 4) and τ' (order 2), with ρ^3 = σ^2 = '-1'. τ' inverts ρ and σ. G^+ is the closed subgroup generated by ρ and σ; it is the image of SL(2,Z)^ ≅ T^+_{1,1}.

On this page:
(3) Assuming G^+ ≠ G, the reflection τ (which has determinant -1) is not in G^+. Hence G = {1,τ}·G^+ is a semidirect product.
(4) This gives the exact sequence 1 → G^+ → G → {±1} → 1, with ε_G the induced 'determinant/orientation character'.
(5) ν_G : G → Z/2Z is the additive version of ε_G.
Convention: the same letter denotes an element of GL(2,Z) (ε_0, ε_1, τ = τ_∞, τ' = τ'_∞, σ = σ_∞, ρ = ρ_∞) and its image in G. Here ε_0, ε_1 are the standard unipotent (Dehn-twist / parabolic) generators.

2°) Definition (6). Z_{ρ,σ} is the set of quadruples (u, μ, ε, ε') in Aut(G^+) × Ẑ* × {±1} × {±1} such that:
- u(ε_0) = ε_0^μ;
- u(ρ) is G^+-conjugate to ρ^{ε'};
- u(σ) is G^+-conjugate to σ^{-ε}.
Z_{ρ,σ} is a subgroup of the product.
(7)-(8) L_ρ and L_σ are the cyclic subgroups generated by ρ and σ. They are quotients of Z/6 and Z/4, and on the next page share the element -1.

In modern terms: for an arbitrary profinite quotient of SL2(Z)^, this is the group of 'inertia-preserving' automorphisms. They act on the parabolic (Dehn twist) ε_0 through a 'cyclotomic' exponent μ ∈ Ẑ*. They preserve the conjugacy classes of the two torsion (elliptic) generators up to inversion, the signs recording that inversion. It is a (1,1)-analogue of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller conditions, i.e. the conditions an element of Gal(Q̄/Q) or GT satisfies when acting on π_1 of the moduli stack M_{1,1}. The elliptic points of orders 4 and 6 (j = 1728, 0) play the role of the branch points, and the cusp plays the role of the inertia at ∞.

The next page shows where this is heading. If G^+ is 'large enough' (ρ not conjugate to ρ^{-1}, σ not conjugate to σ^{-1}, and n ↦ ε_0^n injective on Ẑ; e.g. if G maps onto GL(2,Ẑ)), then the signs and μ are determined by u. Z_{ρ,σ} then embeds in Aut(G^+). The aim is a group of 'Galois-type' symmetries attached to each sufficiently large quotient G, presumably to be compared with the action of Gal(Q̄/Q)/GT on T_{1,1} in the 'équation des lacets' framework.
errors: The deduction 'τ ∉ G^+ since G^+ ≠ G' presupposes G^+ ≠ G as a hypothesis on the quotient G. A profinite quotient of GL(2,Z)^ may well have G^+ = G (e.g. if τ' maps into the image of SL2), so (3)-(4) are not automatic.

Sign conventions are asymmetric: ρ ↦ ρ^{ε'} but σ ↦ σ^{-ε}. Not an error, but it suggests ε is meant to be tied to the orientation/μ-sign (conjugation by τ' inverts σ), while ε' is independent. The intended normalization is not stated on this page.
Notational switch between τ (this page) and τ' (generator chosen on p.547). Harmless since both have determinant -1, but the semidirect splitting (3) with τ requires τ^2 = 1 in G, which is true.

ideas.what: Presentation of GL(2,Z)^ = T^±_{1,1} by ρ, σ, τ' with ρ^6 = σ^4 = τ'^2 = 1, ρ^3 = σ^2, and τ' inverting ρ and σ; orientation exact sequence 1 → G^+ → G → {±1} → 1
ideas.modern_name: amalgam presentation SL2(Z) = Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6 and its extended mapping class group
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Klein, Fricke; Serre's 'Trees' for the amalgam)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses T_{1,1} and the modular tower but not this explicit presentation as far as known

ideas.what: Group Z_{ρ,σ} of automorphisms of a quotient G^+ of SL2(Z)^ acting on the parabolic ε_0 by a Ẑ*-power and preserving the conjugacy classes of the elliptic generators up to sign
ideas.modern_name: 'inertia-preserving' / 'special' outer automorphisms of profinite Γ_{1,1}; (1,1)-level analogue of GT-type conditions (Galois action on π_1(M_{1,1}))
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nakamura; Lochak–Schneps; Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps (1990s) for the Galois/GT action on Γ_{1,1}^ and its conditions
ideas.where_published: Not in published texts; Esquisse only sketches the Teichmüller tower idea

ideas.what: Considering arbitrary profinite quotients G of GL(2,Z)^ that are 'assez gros' (e.g. mapping onto GL(2,Ẑ)) and attaching to each a symmetry group
ideas.modern_name: Galois/GT actions on quotient towers (congruence vs. non-congruence quotients of SL2(Z)^)
ideas.usually_credited_to: various (Ihara, Nakamura, Boggi–Lochak on congruence subgroup problem flavour)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a functorial family of 'GT-type' groups Z_{ρ,σ}(G) attached to every sufficiently large profinite quotient G of GL(2,Z)^. The conditions are a power action on the cusp twist plus preservation, up to sign, of the conjugacy classes of the order-4 and order-6 elliptic elements. The literature studies such conditions mainly for the full Γ_{1,1}^ (or via the GT action), not systematically as a functor on quotients. That would be relevant to Galois actions on non-congruence quotients / dessins on modular curves.
missed.quote: Z_{ρ,σ} ⊂ Aut(G^+) × Ẑ* × {±1} × {±1} ... u(ε_0)=ε_0^μ, u(ρ) conjugué dans G^+ à ρ^{ε'}, u(σ) ... à σ^{-ε}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Gives a uniform framework for Galois/GT symmetries of finite-index (including non-congruence) subgroups of SL2(Z) as orbifold coverings of M_{1,1}. This is an active area (Galois action on modular dessins, non-congruence modular forms), though the basic idea is close to known work.

deep.surprise_reason: Preliminary set-up material: a standard presentation of GL(2,Z)^ and the definition of an inertia/conjugacy-preserving automorphism group for its quotients. It is close in spirit to known work of Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps and Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps on GT acting on Γ_{1,1}. The quotient-wise functorial formulation is a mild unpublished detail, not a surprise.
transcription_corrections: Throughout, 'G' should be the gothic 𝔊 (as in the neighbouring pages): 𝔊, 𝔊^+, ε_𝔊, ν_𝔊.
'(ν_G au-dessus)' is not text: ν_𝔊 labels a curved arrow drawn over the composite 𝔊 → {±1} ≅ Z/2Z.
Margin note reads approximately 'les groupes 𝔊_{ρ,σ}, Z_{ρ,σ}' (left margin beside (6)).
In (6) the symbol after Z_{ρ,σ} appears as '=' / '⊂' with 'def^n' below, i.e. a definition of Z_{ρ,σ} as a subset of the product; the transcription is acceptable.
'(1/2 direct)' = 'semi-direct', written as a fraction-like abbreviation under (3).
Last line of (8): σ^n under L_σ (the handwriting has σ with a hook), consistent with the transcription.
